cards.title: SNAP: Restricting Decoder Expressivity Unlocks Transferable 3D Geometry from Novel View Synthesis
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on 3D representations, agents, or self-supervised vision, SNAP's finding that decoder design—not supervisory signal—is the bottleneck reframes how NVS-based pretraining should be architected.
cards.summary: SNAP is a self-supervised encoder-decoder transformer for novel view synthesis that uses a pose-conditioned local decoder and a latent-space reconstruction target instead of pixel-space targets. Restricting decoder expressivity forces the encoder to retain geometric structure. SNAP competes with geometry-supervised and self-supervised baselines on visual localization, pose estimation, point correspondence, depth estimation, and robot manipulation, with emergent viewpoint invariance despite lower compute and data.

cards.title: 4DCodeBench: New Benchmark Tests Agents on Reconstructing Dynamic Scenes as Executable Code
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers building agents with world-modeling or physical reasoning capabilities, this benchmark directly tests whether frontier models can translate video observations of complex dynamics into working code—a meaningful proxy for causal world understanding.
cards.summary: 4DCodeBench tasks agents with reconstructing dynamic real-world and synthetic scenes—spanning deformation, fluid flow, and fracture—as executable graphics programs via code generation. Benchmarking of frontier models finds that strong static reconstruction ability does not transfer reliably to complex dynamic scene reconstruction, exposing a clear capability gap.

cards.title: Stratified Retention: A Framework for What World Models Should and Shouldn't Forget
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers building continual-learning or world-model systems, this paper formalizes a core oversight: standard forgetting metrics cannot distinguish correct knowledge revision from catastrophic forgetting, creating a flawed evaluation baseline.
cards.summary: The paper argues world models require retention stratified by invariance timescale—physics and object permanence must never be revised, while instance-level facts should be updated as environments change. Standard forgetting metrics rank a frozen model highest, conflating correct revision with failure. The authors propose differential retention, combining invariant regression testing with revision latency measurement, evaluated jointly across the adaptation stream without aggregation.

cards.title: SpiderCSS: ZX-Calculus Pipeline Cuts Logical Error Rates by 33.7% for CSS Fault-Tolerant State Prep
cards.why_it_matters: For engineers and researchers tracking fault-tolerant quantum computing infrastructure, SpiderCSS delivers concrete circuit-level gains—reduced depth, qubit footprint, and error rates—without expensive verification overhead.
cards.summary: SpiderCSS is a compilation pipeline for fault-tolerant logical state preparation in arbitrary CSS codes. Using ZX-calculus and fault-equivalent rewrites, it builds CNOT-minimal circuits provably fault-tolerant without verification circuits. Monte Carlo simulations on codes up to distance 15 show an average 33.7% decrease in logical error rate and a 9.5% increase in acceptance rate versus existing scalable and heuristic methods, with reduced circuit depth and qubit footprint.

cards.title: RNADynBench: 2,585-Trajectory MD Benchmark and Unified Model for RNA Conformational Dynamics
cards.why_it_matters: For ML researchers at the intersection of biology and generative modeling, this benchmark and unified model address both trajectory generation and dynamics representation from a single conformer—a technically underserved problem with clear structural biology implications.
cards.summary: RNADynBench provides 2,585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom MD trajectories with leakage-controlled splits. RNADynNet uses a shared backbone combining coordinate denoising, single-frame-to-trajectory alignment, and physical grounding for both trajectory generation and dynamics fingerprint extraction. Generated trajectories achieve RMSF correlations of 0.875 and 0.766 on standard and high-flexibility test sets respectively; single-conformer predictions show comparable agreement with MD-derived dynamics.

cards.title: Pseudorandom Unitaries May Exist Without Quantum-Computable One-Way Functions: First Oracle Evidence
cards.why_it_matters: This result shifts the foundations of quantum cryptography for researchers in quantum ML and post-quantum security, providing the first evidence PRUs sit in a weaker complexity regime than previously assumed.
cards.summary: The paper proves that five alternating random diagonal phase layers and Hadamard transforms form a strong PRU secure under adaptive access to the unitary, its inverse, transpose, and conjugate. Implemented via a classical random oracle, the construction remains secure against uniform BQP adversaries with QMA-level inversion capability, providing black-box separation evidence that PRUs do not imply quantum-computable one-way functions—strengthening the Kretschmer-Qian-Tal STOC 2025 result.
